articles.title: Real-World Adoption, Use, and Governance of an LLM-Based Electronic Health Record Search and Synthesis Platform
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.08672v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We evaluated the longitudinal adoption and use of Scout, an electronic health record-integrated large language model platform that provides cited search and synthesis of patient records, during staged deployment across a multi-hospital academic health system. Over 11 months, 2,635 users completed 80,465 tasks. 1,768 clinical users initiated use within the first 29 days of system-wide launch, which included a required training. articles.title: Remembering Is Not Enough: Evaluating Timing and Omission in Longitudinal AI Mental Health Support
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.08721v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Evaluations of large language models (LLMs) for mental health support commonly focus on the clinical appropriateness of individual responses, potentially overlooking failures that emerge across extended interactions. articles.summary: arXiv:2611.08749v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Gemini's Nano Banana models, first introduced in late 2025, led to a shift in the capabilities and use of image generation and editing. articles.title: Functional Dependency beyond Similarity: Hierarchical Decomposition of Training Data Attribution in Music Generative Models
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.08839v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Copyright analysis focuses on the similarity between two works. However, generative AI models learn from training data through functional relations beyond similarity. Training Data Attribution (TDA) estimates the influence of each training instance on a generated output and may serve as a basis for remuneration. articles.title: Same Facts, Different Remedy: Linguistic Profiling and Arbitrariness in LLM and System One Decisions
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.08995v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models are increasingly used to resolve consumer complaints, and the way complainants write varies with age, education and socioeconomic status (SES). articles.title: Uniqueness-Aware Feature Engineering for Representing Humans in Algorithmic Decision Making
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.09403v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fairness analyses of algorithmic decision systems typically treat the feature representation of individuals as an a priori fixed input. How well a feature representation captures what is actually decision-relevant for different people and their unique backgrounds, however, is typically left unexamined. We address this gap by modeling feature engineering as a stochastic selection process over the pooled characteristics as candidate features for a finite training population. articles.title: AI Exposure and the Changing Responsibilities in Job Postings
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.09870v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The growing adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) in the workplace has raised questions about how employer demand for different work activities is changing. We examine how the prevalence and content of work activities in online job postings change in association with activity-level measures of AI exposure, derived from Copilot and Claude usage. articles.title: Seeing Is Not Knowing: The Epistemic Limits of LLM-Based Mental Health Inference from Youth Social Media Conversations
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.08565v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Adolescents increasingly use social media for private conversations, sharing experiences and seeking support. These interactions generate digital traces, prompting efforts to infer mental health and psychosocial states. articles.title: Global Solar Siting from Geospatial Embeddings
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.08831v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Global solar photovoltaic (PV) capacity is rapidly growing, helping decrease our emissions and dependence on fossil fuels.
